name: M70 High Precision
verdict: A pair of coupons at 15 s, base 60 s: one with anti-aliasing, one without. No difference to see, even at full resolution; which is which was not marked. Resin use (the anti-aliased one): vat 74.2 -> 71.5 g = 2.7 g, the calibrated estimate held (+3 %). The label says to turn anti-aliasing off.
about: Resione's high-precision standard resin in salmon, made for fine detail.
take: The light goes only shallow into it, so the curl of the strips, not their thickness, set the exposure: 15 s. At that it printed clean 14.5 mm lattice cubes, and anti-aliasing made no difference we could see.

tests.txt: Bars 6-24 s. Up to 12.8 s the bars formed but curled and let go of the film; from 15 s they hold and lie flat. Thickness stops growing at 12.8 s - the light goes only shallow into this resin, as a high-precision one should - so the curl, not the thickness, sets the start: 15 s.
Two coupons at 15 s, one with anti-aliasing and one without. We could not tell them apart, side by side or up close.
Two pairs of 14.5 mm lattice cubes at 15 s: with anti-aliasing on top (one mark), without below (two marks). Clean lattices, and no difference between the pairs that we could see.

The same coupon at 0.10 mm. The exposure is the 0.05 one scaled by the ratio we use for every resin, 20 s, and it printed as well as at 0.05. I broke the tip of the small hammer off by accident afterwards - no matter, it had printed.
